terms.comment: The frost entry has gelū, the freezing itself: Pruīna est, quia nocte gelū fuit. Comenius: rōs congelātus pruīna dīcitur (Orbis pictus 7).

phrases.latin: «Cūr herba alba est?» «Pruīna est, quia nox frīgida fuit.»
phrases.english: “Why is the grass white?” “It’s frost, because the night was cold.”

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 135, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.
